text_fidelity_a: Sunny Health & Fitness Mini Stepper Stair Stepper Exercise Equipment with Resistance Bands This compact stepper is perfect for small spaces.. like a 1 bedroom apartment, studio, or your office!  In my included photo, I place the machine next to my personal paper shredder so that you can see that it's not that big.  The machine came already assembled.  The only thing that I had to do was pull the safety tab from the battery compartment of the digital display, put the display in its designated spot on the machine, attached the resistance bands, and adjust the step height.  Instructions are super simple to follow and the machine itself is easy to use.  You should find an extra battery for the display in the box as well which was great of them to include.  The machine weighs about 14.2 lbs, so I can easily move it around.  I love that it has a display which will tell you the number of steps, the length of time that the steps are done in, and how many calories have been burned.  The display powers on either when the red button on the display is pushed or when the steps are put in motion, and it will auto shut off after not being used for 4 minutes.  You can easily pick up where you left off by powering on the display, and it retains the info until you reset it.  Resetting the display is easy - just press the red button for a few seconds until the display resets.  The instructions do advise you to place an exercise mat under the machine to protect your floors.  I use this machine every day while I watch TV, and I can see toning in my lower abdomen, thighs, and bottom from it.  I do have to admit that I don't use the resistance bands very often, so I just lay those to the side and do the steps, but I do like that I have the option to use them.  I am NOT an exercise enthusiast - I'm getting older & was advised to be active at least 30 minutes/day, so this was an easy solution for me.  The ONLY improvement that I would make to this machine is having a lighted display.  I have a hard time seeing the display while I'm using the machine because it's somewhat dark.
text_fidelity_b: Sunny Health & Fitness Mini Stepper Stair Stepper Exercise Equipment with Resistance Bands

text_fidelity_a:
Srynriwim Collapsible Stool, 2022 Upgraded Portable Folding Stool Lightweight and Sturdy, Indoor Telescopic Stool Non-Slip, Waterproof Camping Stool for Outdoor Fishing Hiking Gardening BBQ(Blue) A bit of a conumdrum here with two ways to look at it. I am 6'3" and currently weigh 225 Lbs. Not a lightweight but as my Pulmonologist informs me "you're no longer clinically obese, you're just obese". Thanks Doc! A left-handed compliment if I ever heard one.

And there lies the rub. The first time I shook this out I had mild difficulty in getting the tabs and latches to hook up-- like I did just now. That seems to inspire a little less confidence in how safely it will support me without crashing down. Once it is expanded and set up it appears to be pretty sturdy. The color also makes it easy to see in the yard.

But having just had double knee replacement I was a bit concerned that it would hold me without making me faceplant in the yard. When I asked my wife to watch me sit on it in the kitchen she said "don't do that!". The sight of me pulling it out and clicking it together didn't inspire confidence in her either.

It did hold me while sitting still although I was a bit reluctant to shift my weight around on it. That would be my major sticking point. On a yard that is not completely level I know that I would have to be careful. The other part of that is that leaning forward or to one side suddenly puts additional stress on whichever part of the base is sitting on the ground. I am not convinced that leaning over wouldn't cause the stool to buckle and me to fall over.

So there it is. It seems to be a smart design and should solve the problem of having a stool available when needed. However plastic is not indestructible and will often bend as it is stressed over and over again. Good idea, decent execution, but it doesn't inspire any confidence for someone my size.
text_fidelity_b: Srynriwim Collapsible Stool, 2022 Upgraded Portable Folding Stool Lightweight and Sturdy, Indoor Telescopic Stool Non-Slip, Waterproof Camping Stool for Outdoor Fishing Hiking Gardening BBQ(Blue)

I received a brain injury over 9 years ago, and am relearning how to do everything. I also live in the country, without a car, and many miles from a store. Normally I would have AAA batteries, but I could not find any the night I decided to install these awesome lights and try to navigate this bike I just bought. A man in my 50's should know better, and I have some around somewhere, but I had to wait to try out my new investment.

Imagine my disappointment when the first whistle that I tried wasn't that loud. It just gave a muffled sort of whistle. It would probably be loud enough if I blew as hard as I could, though. Since I only need three of these for my intended uses, happily, the other three are nearly as loud as I expected. I was hoping this would be something that would scare off potential attackers or draw attention and help from nearby, and I think it will do that. I'm giving one to each family member and, as we live on a farm, I need the sound to carry for quite some distance. The intent is to get attention if someone is hurt. We and our neighbors have had problems in the past were yelling for help couldn't be heard, but hopefully these will be. I like the lanyards, which have a satiny feel (which should be comfortable on the skin) and an easy-to-work toggle.

The whistle is 2 3/16" long and 5/8" wide and 3/8" deep, so they don't take up that much room. They are lightweight. The lanyard is about 16 inches long when major doubled, lying flat (from the back of the neck to the whistle rather than the length from the whistle all the way around that point again).

text_fidelity_a:
Park Tool Machine Thread Storage Hook I was specifically looking for a hook application like this that was bolted, rather than using a large lag screw. I have a relatively open attic above my garage with 2x4 joists and wanted to use this hook to hang ladders and my bike from the ceiling. I had looked at the smaller, and larger hook, and I believe this is a good compromise between price and size (not too small to make hanging things harder, not too large to be cumbersome). The rubber coating is very thick and seems very durable.

One thing not mentioned is the thread type. It is an M10-1.5. What I plan on doing is locating the hook in the ceiling of my finished garage from below. Then, utilizing a nut coupler with a ~3" bolt and some washers, securing through a perpendicular 2"x4" horizontally laid across my vertical 2"x4" truss chords.

I have used lag screw hooks in the past and I was never confident they would hold, or if they were centered properly, etc. If you have an open attic, and a finished garage, I think this is the proper application.
text_fidelity_b: Park Tool Machine Thread Storage Hook

Aerobie Superdisc (6044022) My Black Lab can't get enough Frisbee, she demands it at least twice a day. Unlike the flying discs made specifically for dogs, these fly just like a real Frisbee (both in distance and flight pattern) yet have the soft rim so the dog"s mouth isn't injured when she catches it in mid-air. The brightly colored rim makes them easy to find when my throwing gets too wild and they end up somewhere she can't get to. The rim is squared off and ever so slightly raised above the actual disc which makes it easier for her to pick up if it lands flat on a slick or level surface.

I have tried many versions of Frisbees through the last 40 years of Labs in my life and these are by far the best. The one I just had to throw out was over 5 years old and eventually cracked in half but up until then flew perfectly despite being riddled with teeth marks, dents, and small cracks.

Weighted Jump Rope - (1LB) Solid PVC for Crossfit and Boxing - Heavy Jump Rope with Memory Non-Slip Cushioned Foam Grip Handles for Fitness Workouts Endurance and Strength Training Life recently changed and as I searched for ways to stay in shape I found an old cheap jump rope in the closet. After 3 weeks of trying, with some moderate success, I realized that the rope I was using was holding me back. I needed a longer, heavier, sturdier rope.
I spent a good amount of time comparing reviews. I just got back from a workout with this product.

1. The rope is easily adjustable. I am 6'4" and it is a good height for me, but others who are average height will need to adjust. You will need basic tools (phillips screw driver and strong cutters), but you can always ask a handy friend or family member to help.
2. The rope is thick, and the handles are large. They work perfectly for me, but if you have small hands or issues with hand/joint pain you may want to take that into consideration.
3. The product is made out of good quality plastic. It shows signs of wearing from the first use, but that is to be expected. I would warn people to be careful and not throw this on the ground, the handles would likely easily crack/break or cause gouges out of the plastic that could be painful on your hands.
4. The rope is 1.5 pounds, and the weight is in the ROPE.
5. The rope performs well, is sturdy, and offers good swing and feedback. You can easily slow down or speed up as you're jumping, and the rope keeps a nice arc even on windy days.
6. One reviewer said this left red marks on their legs, I don't see how anyone could do that with this rope without some intention. It does weigh 1.5 pounds though and is fast, so be careful of your surroundings.

Overall this is a good purchase and addition to my isolation routine. I wanted a solid $30 option, and this product fit the bill.
text_fidelity_b: Weighted Jump Rope - (1LB) Solid PVC for Crossfit and Boxing - Heavy Jump Rope with Memory Non-Slip Cushioned Foam Grip Handles for Fitness Workouts Endurance and Strength Training

text_fidelity_a:
LifeSpan TR1200i Folding Treadmill A four star rating. I have to qualify that. If all I want is a standalone machine to work out on, this is a five star machine. But, the Fitness Club and computerized system - junk as far as I have figure it out.

I delayed reviewing for two years to make sure I could do a good review.

For walking or running, it is smooth and reliable. I like the many different workout profiles shifting speed and incline and they stand the test of time. If that is all you want, buy this machine.

But, they ship it without a USB storage device when using USB is supposed to be central to using the Fitness Club and better managing your workout and physical fitness.

So I bought a USB stick and followed instructions. The machine has never uploaded a workout to the stick following all the instructions. And frankly, that makes this machine worthless for fitness management. The interactivehealthpartner website would be a good tool if I could just get the link between machine and computer to work. Several calls to the company and I got the idiot treatment.

So, summary, I can't recommend or not recommend this machine. I assume there is an included cost for the membership and electronic brains of this machine and membership. Thus, for just a machine I would look for something cheaper. For a machine with all the bells and whistles, I'd buy something else that really works and at least includes a 5 dollar USB stick!
text_fidelity_b: LifeSpan TR1200i Folding Treadmill

You can’t change the toes stops out, but if you try, you will have to take the plate off to reattach the toe stop because the nut is loosely in the plate. The toe stops will disintegrate after about a month (4-5 practices) from use. The wheels are crap and you can’t replace the bearings. Well designed!! I have 2 other infuser bottles. I never use them. At first I thought what an idea! But I only used each bottle once. Who knows where they are now? Those 2 infusers leaked around the caps & were just smooth on the sides - so I would drop the bottles. My new Zoma bottle doesn't leak & it has a different type of grip on each of 2 sides. I haven't dropped it yet!
I like the way the top is designed also. It has a slick twist to lock & unlock pop-up cap. I haven't seen a cap quite like this! Plus, it took me only 1 minute (1 second?) to figure it out!
I like that instructions were included with the bottle. Sounds simple but I learned that to release some of the natural flavor that you muddle (smash) some of the fruit. Duh! Sounds fundamental but I missed that with my other bottles. I put some frozen cherries in one of my old bottles . They just sat there & looked faded & disgusting. They lost their color but none of their flavor came out. The instructions also give you some great combinations to use. I think my favorite is cucumber water - so refreshing!. I love my new infuser bottle!
I did receive this at a reduced cost for an honest opinion. Thank You!

text_fidelity_a:
Segway Ninebot S Smart Self-Balancing Electric Scooter, 800W Motor (Ver.S MAX 1000), 13.7 Miles Range(Ver.S MAX 23.6)& 10MPH(Ver.S MAX 12.4), Hoverboard w/t LED Light, Compatible with Gokart Kit First - the battery life is nowhere near what it claims. Just now I went to an appointment and the app says its got 7.2 miles range left. My appointment is 1.3 miles away so I figure 2.6 round trip, this thing should be able to handle it. Well, it dies on the way there. This is ridiculous - the app needs to be IN THE BALLPARK. NOW what really really ticks me off: they made this thing for CHILDREN cause this thing is a nightmare for me, 5'10'' man, to navigate in 'luggage mode' after the battery gets to be too low to ride...it's swerving left and right every other second, i'm kicking it repeatedly, each foot getting swiped and knicked and knocked, stuttering my steps and really Throwing off my walking and bumping into everything - I'm incredibly sore. My hip hurts now, feet hurt, heels hurt, knees hurt, shins hurt, hand hurts.... my lower back hurts from having to bend over because they didn't have the good sense to make the handle just a couple inches longer. It's TERRIBLE and just plain stupid. So any time i saved by riding was completely eaten up by having to lug it back - all. because the app is entirely unreliable, inaccurate, and the machine poorly designed.

the plastic is poor quality - things breaking off. The knee bar has broken 3 times!

THE WORST PART!!! the updates slow the machine down from 12 to 10mph. it feels like a mobile device for an elderly person now. 2mph makes a huge difference. and one of the things destroying my range is that it pushes back, trying to throw you off the machine. Literally. It thinks you're going too fast (when historically, those were acceptable speeds) and now it just throws you backwards. You have to completely stop and pause for it to reset it. Otherwise it is tilting BACKWARD - uncomfortable and DANGEROUS. esp so since the kneepads are now behind your knees so you have practically zero control over the machine. and lets not forget: thats eating up your battery. so you're wasting battery, to get there slower, all while being incredibly less safe and comfortable. How dumb could these people possibly be???

For $70 you can buy 3rd party software that turns off most of the STUPID TILTING BACKWARDS NONSENSE and gives back a few mph ....just ridiculous i have to pay extra for that and that its not included in the app.

These guys ruined their own machine and made it unreliable and unsafe.
text_fidelity_b: Segway Ninebot S Smart Self-Balancing Electric Scooter, 800W Motor (Ver.S MAX 1000), 13.7 Miles Range(Ver.S MAX 23.6)& 10MPH(Ver.S MAX 12.4), Hoverboard w/t LED Light, Compatible with Gokart Kit

text_fidelity_a:
DeskCycle Ellipse Under Desk Elliptical Machine - Get Fit While You Work with Our Compact Mini Seated Elliptical Machine - Burn Calories, Boost Energy, Tone Muscles, and Increase Productivity I really love this for what it can do, but I want to address my issues with it first. It's heavier than the photos show - picking up to move it is not easy. It's also bigger than I thought. It fits under my desk ok, but your desk needs to be pretty deep to be able to use it ergonomically. My chair wheels easily hit this if I am close enough to type comfortably. So I try to use it only for breaks when I don't need to type. However, since it's there, I tend to just use it and end up moving my butt about halfway up my chair so I can reach the keyboard easier without causing RSI. I found that actually works my thigh muscles a little more anyway. It's actually hard for me to just stop pedaling and let my legs & feet rest! I also do not know how o register the activity on my Fitbit, so I will research that. I use it sporadically throughout the day, so stopping to set the time is not an option.
SO for the benefits - my blood sugar is staying down thanks to the movement, even when I have to work! My restless legs are improving - I think movement actually helps those muscles relax more. I can actually focus more on my work when I'm not thinking I should go for a walk or get up and move.
This is super quiet! I expected some noise, but it's not bad at all. It's easy to adjust the tension. I wasn't sure why the feet pedals were so long, but I like being able to place them in different areas for different muscles. It really does make a difference where you place your feet.
Overall, I really like it!
text_fidelity_b: DeskCycle Ellipse Under Desk Elliptical Machine - Get Fit While You Work with Our Compact Mini Seated Elliptical Machine - Burn Calories, Boost Energy, Tone Muscles, and Increase Productivity

text_fidelity_a:
CamelBak eddy Glass Water Bottle, 24oz I am SO HAPPY that they finally made a glass Camelbak!! I have it in blue but will be getting it in every color because I'm so excited they finally gave me what I wanted. For a couple of years now I had been using a kerplunk glass bottle and just placing the camelbak top/straw on it. But it didn't fit quite right. This bottle is great. There's no plasticy or metal taste to the water. Glass is the only material that doesn't leach a seperate taste to the water after it's been in there for a while. The only thing is that the straw is still plastic. I actually have some straws made out of glass that I sometimes use with the camelbaks, and they work, but again- there is a fit issue so I often can't use them. I wish camelbak would make a stainless steel version of their straw.

UPDATE/ March 2013: for those who are interested, I found a company that makes custom sized glass straws. It's called "GLASS DHARMA" and they have a website. If you order their "smoothie" sized straws and ask that they be custom cut to 7 & 3/8 inches, they will fit great with these camelbaks. I've been using their glass straws for years and they are really durable- last forever if you don't drop them on a hard floor (they are glass after-all), but this is the first time I realized they did custom sizes so I measured and ordered a couple and they fit/work great! Their straws come with a life-time guarantee. I even dropped my camelbak on the floor once and luckily it didn't break, but I lifted the lid and checked the glass straw to make sure it was fine- not a scratch. If you decide to use these you should wet the glass straw and inside of the camelbak lid before twisting the straw in- The lubrication will make it slide in without you having to worry about being too rough. The straws hold up perfectly inside these camelbaks. (Oh- and since they are glass I wouldn't use them in bottles that you use for sports activities or anything like that.) They look cooler than the plastic straws too because you can see the cloudy white plastic straw through the bottle vs the crystal-clear glass straw that matches better with the bottle (and the water).

I still use the plastic straw when I leave the house so that I don't have to worry about breakage during transport etc... but when I drink indoors (which is 99% of the time for me) I use these glass straws instead. The plastic straw is ok- unlike when I use plastic bottles which give off a plasticy taste almost immediately- the straw only seems to leech a plasticy taste if it's been sitting in the water for a couple of days or more... but Still I like to avoid plastic whenever possible and if you are like me you might appreciate this alternative too.
text_fidelity_b: CamelBak eddy Glass Water Bottle, 24oz

1. It DOESN'T have an SOS mode (thank you, Suboos). Simple button cycles through low/med/high/off.

All things considered the "cons" outweigh the "pros" so I give it a thumbs-down.

text_fidelity_a: Fishpond Westwater Guide Lumbar Pack - Steelhead/Pacific I really, really wanted this bag to work. I love my other Fishpond gear. Everything I've owned from them is very well thought out and cleverly designed. This pack has great potential. I like the simplicity, the fact that it has a few dividers inside and plenty of lash points outside. It's also very comfortable to wear. HOWEVER, the point of this bag is to be water resistant and it completely fails on that front. While the actual material seems good, the zippers let in water immediately, even without being submerged. The worst part is not even that water gets into the bag - it's that the water collects and pools at the bottom of the main compartment and in the small front compartment and is difficult to clear. Even after shaking the bag upside down and running a cloth through it, there was still water tucked in the corners and edges of the pockets that I just couldn't get out. It took a long time to air dry. As I mentioned above, I love my other Fishpond gear, including another hip pack (that has since been discontinued). I bought this bag solely because I wanted something that would keep my things dry in a rainstorm. Unfortunately, it just won't.

text_fidelity_a:
Steiner Sports MLB New York Yankees Authentic Yankee Stadium "Freeze Dried Grass" Sod w/ Glass Display Case I should have listened to the other 2 reviewers. I am beyond disappointed in the condition of this item. First of all, the fact that all the pieces were separate would not have been an issue IF the items were packed properly. The piece of sod was thrown haphazardly into a very thin plastic bag that was completely wide open and not secured closed at all. There is almost as much dirt and grass in the bottom of the bag as there is on the piece of sod. I'm surprised that there isn't dirt and grass all over the box it was thrown into as well. Worst of all, the sod is absolutely NOTHING like the picture. it is a 3 inch round piece of mostly dirt, that is not a rich dark brown as pictured, but a dried-out, tan-colored crumbling mess. And, the grass is long, sparse and a mix of pale green, yellow and brown. Not sure what the freeze-drying process is supposed to do, but the grass and dirt are so dry that you can't even breathe near it without pieces of grass and dirt falling off. What a mess! AND it smells pretty nasty too.

The letter of authenticity is trash (or at least it is to Steiner). It was thrown into the box along with the packing materials, without an envelope or any other protection. From being jostled around inside the shipping box, it is now crumpled and torn in at least three places along the side. Granted, it is a thicker-weight paper, but an envelope would have been nice (especially for the price). The letter says that the sod was removed on March 14, 2009 and that it is "unconditionally guaranteed" - whatever that means. It's difficult to tell if the signature of "Brandon Steiner" is signed in ink or a copy. I don't want to damage the signature trying to figure it out.

The case is actually a baseball case and comes in a "single baseball glass case" box. When I first opened the shipping box, I thought I'd been sent the wrong item. The case IS made of glass, not acrylic, and supposedly has a cherry wood base. It also is not nearly as nice as the picture depicts. The wood is dry and dull and the joints are roughly glued together and uneven. Unlike one of the other reviewers (and the description), I did not receive a separate sticker to apply to the base. It actually has a metal plaque already attached. The problem is, the only words that are legible are "Yankee Stadium Artifact." There are three full lines of smaller writing below that but it is completely unreadable. I can't tell if the words got scratched off or if it was improperly printed on the plate to begin with. I cannot read what it says at all.

I'm not familiar with these types of cases, but there is nothing that holds the grass in place. The bottom is a slick mirror, and the slightest movement causes the sod to slide around inside the case, leaving dirt and debris all over the bottom. Unless its kept perfectly still, it will probably fall apart completely into a big mess in no time. My biggest regret is that I did not purchase this from Amazon. I paid only $59 from another source who is not nearly as easy to deal with. Although, I don't think it would have made a difference in the quality of the product or awful packaging, because this item ships directly from Steiner sports anyway.

I've posted over 80 product reviews on Amazon. This is the first time I've ever felt the need to post pictures or video. This item is so pathetic - you really have to see it to believe it, so I am going to post something tomorrow. I just wanted to post my review ASAP so that anyone considering buying this as a last-minute Christmas gift is forewarned. I initially felt too embarrassed to give this as a gift, but now I think the recipient might appreciate the "tragic humor" of this item. It would make a good conversation piece for sure! I will let him decide if he wants to return it for something else, or keep it as something to show to his friends and laugh about.
text_fidelity_b: Steiner Sports MLB New York Yankees Authentic Yankee Stadium "Freeze Dried Grass" Sod w/ Glass Display Case

Still, pretty quickly this knife has made it into my rotation.  The main reason is its ease of use.  The washers have worn in quite well and though it was a bit stiff out of the box, within a week, it opens like butter.. I've typically always favored old-school slipjoint pocket knives over locking knives for carry, but i really see the ease of one-hand use in this design.  The weight and size of the blade also really add to the inertia upon opening so it's just a really satisfying knife to flip open.. Other people might balk at the grips- I thought they felt a little cheap in the hand when I first inspected the knife, but they've turned out to be pretty solid, textured just enough to prevent slippage if they got wet.  Is it the best knife for the money?  I don't know- I bought mine for around 15 bucks and at that price wasn't expecting much:  Just a decent linerlock with a soft enough blade to easily keep sharp- something for the car-  but its size, ease of use and just good solid blade design make for a really practical tool knife which i carry more and more.
text_fidelity_b: Ontario Knife Rat-1 Knife, 5in. Closed

It counts steps, distance, calories. Don't ask me if they are all accurate. I'm only tracking steps and working towards a goal.
You can look back up to a week of steps, in case you are keeping track.
It resets every midnight (no, it never turns off).
Small enough to fit in a pocket.
The cons:
Well, con. Only one up to now. I tried hooking it to my bra or neckline (sometimes I wear dresses) and it doesn't record steps very accurately. I'll be walking for 10 minutes and the number of steps doesn't change. So on dress days, I hook it to my purse, or my underwear if the dress is baggy.

I knew that when I got it.  It gives an added feeling of security when you are getting used to the chair.  I plan to remove mine later when I am comfortable with the feel of the chair. I also like the fact that the balls are simple and cheap to replace if I wear one out.  I won't be shelling out $300 for a chair that lasts two years.  Cheaper chairs last even less. text_fidelity_a:
MinnKota Riptide 55 ST Bowmount Trolling Motor with i-Pilot and No Foot Pedal (55lbs Thrust, 54" Shaft) I bought one of these for my 18' Carolina Skiff. I also bought the quick release mount. I bought the quick release mount so I could remove the trolling motor when travelling long distances with the boat. I fish from MD to the Gulf and bouncing down the road wouldn't be be good for it. First impression is that I'm going to like it a lot. I've been in the water twice using the trolling motor, both times in salt water, which is where I spend most of my fishing time. Installation was easy and deploying and retracting the ST55 is also easy. The iPilot anchor function worked well in 1.5 mph currents and 12 knot winds. I'll try it in the 8kt currents in the OBX in August. I like the iPilot control unit and no foot pedal because I'm not restricted to a certain place in the boat. I maxed it out and was surprised at how strong the motor was. I used the motor for about 2 hours and battery drain was about 1.4 volts from 14.2 to 12.8. Totally acceptable, especially for the size boat and winds. The instructions call for a 60 amp inline circuit breaker, however, I'm using a 40 amp and it was fine on full power. I've given it a 4 star rating right now and will return to add more to this review once I've used the programming features of the iPilot.

Update 24 Feb 15: I have nothing but praise for Min-Kota and the RipTide ST55. I've put about 70 hours on this motor and spent many hours in the anchor mode against 2-3 knot tides. I didn't use my boat anchor once during the summer and fall months because the RipTide's anchor function is spot on. I mainly fish in saltwater and I've used it from Florida, to North Carolina, to Maryland and its performance is outstanding. The only down side is it doesn't have automatic deploy and retrieve. I know Min-Kota is working on one. I love the iPilot! I can use it from anywhere on the boat and only have to remember when facing backwards, left is right and right is left. Duh. Most definitely 5 STARS
text_fidelity_b: MinnKota Riptide 55 ST Bowmount Trolling Motor with i-Pilot and No Foot Pedal (55lbs Thrust, 54" Shaft)

text_fidelity_a:
Ferexer 48 oz Sports Borosilicate Glass Water Bottle with Bamboo Lid with Neoprene Sleeve CONTEXT:
After watching a documentary about teflon and plastic etcetera, and learning that all similar products leech into the water, I opted to start using glass. After using a Hydro, I was a little bit bummed that my water wouldn't be cold AF for hours on end, but I figured it was worth the sacrifice. I have smaller glass bottles, but with as much as I workout, I needed a way to track and increase my intake. I found this one and immediately needed it because of its size!

PROS:
- The neoprene sleeve it comes with actually does a pretty good job of keeping the water cold AND helps with keeping the condensation at bay. It never gets soaking wet.
- It holds so much water! One bottle of this a day is one 1.4 liters.
- Water just tastes so much better. I don't care what anyone says... water tastes better out of glass.
- The handle addition on the neoprene is a huge plus! It helps with lugging this thing around.

CONS:
- This isn't really a con for me, BUT I know it will be for others. The water doesn't stay cold for hours... I live in Hawaiʻi, so naturally, it gets warm pretty quick (but keep reading for tips). If you live somewhere cold, like Washington, I don't think you'll really have a problem. :)
- Obviously, this bottle is pretty freakin large. So carrying it around can be a b-word.

TIPS:
- I learned that putting ice in my bottle helps a lot with keeping it cold throughout the day (not even kidding). I usually fill the bottle with 1/4 ice and the rest with filtered water. By the time I am getting to the bottom of my bottle, the ice has melted, but the water is still cold.

OVERALL:
I can't recommend this bottle enough. It is perfect for me!
text_fidelity_b: Ferexer 48 oz Sports Borosilicate Glass Water Bottle with Bamboo Lid with Neoprene Sleeve

text_fidelity_a:
Intex Challenger Kayak, Inflatable Kayak Set with Aluminum Oars and High Output Air-Pump Grabbed one of these on sale on Black Friday, and finally got to try it out. Goes together easily and not difficult to pump up. One person can carry it, though it's less awkward for two. Between the netting on the front and the stowage in the stern behind the seat, we were able to take all our stuff with us and not have to worry about possible pilferage.

The instructions are a bit vague, so take note that there are TWO chambers to inflate, and the first one to be inflated is NOT the obvious top chamber (with the number 2 beside it), but the hidden number 1 chamber, which is located on the starboard (right) side, inside wall above the floor and a little aft of the middle of the boat. Each valve has two lids, one on top of the other; undo the upper one (with the 4-lobed lid) to inflate, and undo the lower lid (larger and round) to deflate. Don't over tighten the upper lid, or it's difficult to open it without the bottom lid opening too, and losing air. You may hear a hissing sound while inflating the second chamber, but don't worry—the air passage narrows at one point and it tends to hiss while filling; you're not actually losing the air.

Had a little trouble with back support on the front seat—next time I'll bring a rolled towel to support my lower back. It's good to bring a towel anyway so you can dry off the kayak before deflating and storing it. I suggest before taking the boat out you inflate it, test for leaks and do a test-sit to figure out how you want to arrange the seats and straps ahead of time; then use a sharpie to indicate who the seat is adjusted for, and where it needs to be stuck on the velcro.

Be gentle with the pump and paddles; some reviews mentioned they broke easily, though they seem sturdy enough to me—I don't think they'll stand up to much abuse, though.

Lots of fun for the price!

P.S: If you don't have PFDs, the ONYX MoveVent Dynamic Paddle Sports Life Vest (sold elsewhere on Amazon) works very well, and doesn't get in your way when paddling. Don't forget to buy a couple of paddle leashes with carabiners, too!
text_fidelity_b: Intex Challenger Kayak, Inflatable Kayak Set with Aluminum Oars and High Output Air-Pump

text_fidelity_a: Hilleberg Soulo Camping Tent I am only writing a review because there is none here.  When another review becomes available, mine should be removed.  This tent is a little bit heavy for a backpacker, particularly one going long distances.  It is also expensive compared to many tents.  Not everyone will like that.  Here in the west, the winds can be terrible any time, and it is possible to get true severe snow in almost any season, even at high summer.  In view of extreme wind likelihood and snow possibility, it is a good idea to get a very strong tent.  Both by its shape and construction details, this is very strong.  It is poor economy to think the tent has too high a price.  It is made with great thought into every detail, even the materials and the details of how stitching is done.  So, if someone does a particularly good and thoughtful job, it is the wrong idea to refuse to pay them for good work.  That is realistic, at least to me.  Yes.  When a less well made tent shreds in the wind and blows off into the distance, a person will not think this too high a price.
text_fidelity_b: Hilleberg Soulo Camping Tent

text_fidelity_a:
Usitek Fitbit Flex 2 Accessory Bands for Fitbit Flex 2 / Fitbit Flex2,Silicone Fitness Replacement Accessories Wrist Band for 2016 New Fitbit Flex 2 with Steel Buckle,Pack of 3. My husband and I are really happy with these replacement bands (reasons detailed below). Ideally, honestly we would give them a 4.5/5 star rating if possible due to one flaw (lining up of the lights) but otherwise, they are great and we would both recommend!

Look: We got the black, grey, and blue bands and we both really like the colors. Although the black is standard with FitBit Flex2, the dark blue costs extra, so I really like that we can get all three colors here. One thing I can say about the colors though is that the blue band looks much darker in person than on the photo (although, I actually like it better in real life than on the photo). It's not really a big deal, but I think the different color makes it look just a little more professional and a little less like a typical fitness band. And, since there are three bands, you have choice and can change up your band as you change up your outfits!

Feel: I really like how soft the rubber/silicone material is. It is not stiff (as I have found other after market fitness bands to be), nor is it "sticky" (sometimes rubber can catch fine hairs on the arm and feel like it's ripping them out....that is NOT the case with this band!) The clasp on the back is comfortable and doesn't push into the wrist. Overall, it is very soft and comfortable to wear both during the day and at night.

Fit: there are two aspects here- first how the FitBit Flex2 fits into the band and how the band fits on the wrist. The FitBit fits nicely into the "pouch" left for it- it is secure (does not feel like it will fall out) but is not difficult to get it in either. One of my (only) complaints, however, is that the holes on the bands do not line up PERFECTLY with the lights on the FitBit. Honestly, this is such a minor thing and most people might not even notice it at all. I think it's actually largely because the rubber/silicone is a little bit thicker on this band than it is on the normal band, so it looks a little further away, so depending on your angle when you look at it might look like the entire light isn't on (but I have to say you can always tell which light is on or off, it never covers a light or makes it impossible to see- I think I might be slightly anal retentive to even notice!!). As far as the wrist fit goes...I'm actually really impressed here. It fit my husband without a problem and it even fit my (super dainty) wrists in the second to smallest hole! I feel comfortable to say that this would fit (almost) any adult's wrist. There's no need to keep multiple bands around- one size will definitely fit all.

Security and Protection: Although I have never (ever) worried that the clasp on my Fitbit will wear down and I might eventually lose my FitBit, I can see how that might happen (particularly after long periods of wear and removal to charge). Either way, this band removes any slight concern about that fact with the steel (watch like) clasp. It is obvious this clasp will not accidentally loosen and fall off. Ever. I also like that it feels soft and like it will protect my FitBit in case I (inevitably) bang it into something. The band provides enough protection that I won't break it. That being said, one difference between these bands and the band that comes with is the holes (to view the lights) are open on these bands whereas the are covered with a piece of clear plastic on the regular band it comes with. I'm not sure how much protection that clear plastic provides (I tend to find dust and things on the FitBit regardless), but something to mention.

The Fridge Drink Cooler - Lifoam If you like cold drinks, this is the ultimate coozie to get! They not only keep your drinks cold for hours, but they can actually make your drinks colder than they were from the refrigerator!

That is because each coozie has two main layers that work together to chill the drinks: an inner gel layer and a thick outer styrofoam layer.

When you put the coozie in the freezer, the gel layer freezes. This layer can actually drop the temperature of whatever drink you put int the coozie. It's like wrapping your drink in a blanket of ice! Then the styrofoam layer makes sure all that great coldness stays there. Drinks normally stay cold for several hours!

Another nice feature when using these coozies is that there is no problem with leaving wet rings on the furniture because the coozies prevent the normal condensation problem you have with cold drinks in a warm environment. I think this is because of the thick insulation layer. The cold inside is insulated from the warm outside which prevents condensation.

I know these coozies last for years. I originally found these coozies on MisterCold.com in 2006 and used them constantly ever since. I have taken them with me everywhere I go. They have held up very well for so much use. After 7 years of use, they finally began to show signs of wear (slight fraying at the bottom) so I decided it was time to get new ones. I was thrilled to find them here on Amazon! The new ones I got are just as good, if not better, than the original ones I bought years ago.

If you want to enjoy drinks that are cold, cold, cold and stay that way for hours, this is the perfect item for you. Just be sure to get a bunch because once your family and friends try them, they'll use them all the time. So you need plenty on hand to be sure there's always a cold one waiting for you! The rule in my house is you can use them as long as you don't take the last one. That way there's always at least one chilled and ready to go!

I followed directions explicitly and with extreme attention to detail. On a recent trip to the range it was time to exercise my 380ACP. When I removed it from the holster the top rail was covered in rust. I keep this particular model in my glove compartment and always run my air conditioner. When I saw the rust I was shocked and started wiping it off immediately before realizing I should be taking photo's. On May 6th I sent a letter with photographs to FrogLube demanding an explanation. My letter, sent via FedEx, was received May 9th. As of today there's been no response what so ever. In my opinion, FrogLube is a fraud and I'll be converting my collection back to traditional products. Do not believe what you see, hear and read about FrogLube; don't buy FrogLube, and tell your friends as soon as possible!

Sportsvoutdoors Trekking Pole, Telescopic Collapsible Anti-Shock Climbing Stick With EVA Handle for Hiking/Walking/Trekking (Black) I could have gotten something similar to this telescopic cane locally, and for nearly the same price. But this one appeared to have some advantages the others didn't. There wasn't any instructions on using this cane, but it wasn't too hard to figure out. To adjust the length there are three sections which can be pulled out to make the cane longer. The cane in it's fully collapsed state is 21" long, fully extended its 42". To change the lengths you twist the shafts which loosen or tighten the assembly depending on the direction you twist. You can actually pull out a section completely if you're not careful (it slips back in pretty easily). The tip of the cane is interesting. There is a rubber foot that can be removed which exposes a small diameter metal point, that I assume is for use on icy surfaces (we don't get that too often here in Texas). There is another thing that can be screwed on the end of the cane, some sort of round dome looking thing, I haven't a clue what it's purpose might be.

Over-all I happy with the walking stick, I like that it collapses down like it does for easy storage & carrying. And that it feels like pretty solid support when in use. I'm happy with my purchase.

text_fidelity_a:
Explorer K2 Kayak, 2-Person Inflatable Kayak Set with Aluminum Oars, Manual and Electric Pumps… For under 100 bucks shipped you get everything you need to get out on the water minus life vests. The skeg has been improved as it now has a new locking mechanism and silhouette. The 86" paddles are well made for the price, nicely curved, have an adjustable paddle angle and float (as we found out accidentally) so paddle leashes are recommend. The boat is stable when inflated properly using the pressure gauge "measuring strip" and did not rock too bad when standing up in the aft position with an adult seated up front. The boat has a drain plug in the stern which has to be closed as mine was shipped in the open position. The 30 gauge PVC (Vinyl) has a nylon like backing and appears to be rugged enough for large lakes and mild moving waters. Not sure I would personally use this on class III+ water but some reviewer's have reported their own success stories. It tracks well on flat water with the skeg and okay with a peaceful river current without. Seats are more comfortable than I originally imagined when purchasing. Watch out for over inflation as we pumped her up at 64° and by the afternoon the temp had increased to 74° which caused the inflation gauge to read 5-10% (0.5-1 cm) higher due to air expansion. Over all I am impressed for the cost of purchase. It comes with one 3"x3" self adhesive patch similar to "Tear-Aid type B" (looks like a square piece of yellow card stock) and two 2" clear patches that require you to use your own PVC cement. The pump tube can be stored inside the pump itself by unscrewing the end and coiling it around the pump shaft. It packs up into a Blackhawk tactical bag that I have as the Intex bag was uncomfortable to carry since it didn't have a shoulder strap. The boat is 22.2 lbs without the seats, 25.8 lbs with both seats not including other accessories. Takes about 10 minutes to setup with the included air pump or 5 minutes with the 12v Intex pump (which has deflate mode too!!!).

Things to remember include closing the drain plug and monitoring inflation to prevent over inflation related seam tears. If you know the temp will increase throughout the day by 5-10° i would recommend under inflating by 5-10% (0.5-1 cm) on the inflation gauge which is approximately 10 cm long when fully inflated.
text_fidelity_b: Explorer K2 Kayak, 2-Person Inflatable Kayak Set with Aluminum Oars, Manual and Electric Pumps…

text_fidelity_a: Seesii Stopwatch with Whistle,Multifunctional Digital Timer Supports Split Timing, Alarm Clock Function, Sports Stopwatch Suitable for Sports, Fitness Coaches and PE Teachers and Referees A stopwatch in my opinion should have 2 functions.  One that starts and stops the clock starting from zero and one feature that counts down from a set number of minutes or seconds and then alerts you when the countdown timer reaches zero.  This stopwatch only has the first feature where the time starts at zero and stops when you manually stop it (and that btw works well).  It is missing the countdown feature that I actually need for timing 1 minute sparring match, a 2 minute wrestling match, a 1 and a half minute boxing match for example.  Instead, it has a clock with the time of day and an alarm feature, like it's a portable alarm clock.  Why would I need a wakeup or reminder alarm clock in a stopwatch?  Also, I don't know how to power it of nor do I know how to change the battery which according to the manual, it says it's a CR2032 3V.  The manual is a little confusing too.  I do not recommend this product at all.

text_fidelity_a:
Schwinn Fitness 430 Elliptical Trainer [Discontinued] I researched ellipticals for quite a while before ordering the Schwinn 430. My friend, Tom, also researched this type of equipment until his eyes fell out of his head. He wound up buying the Sole for about twice the cost of the Schwinn. In any event, he recommended the Schwinn as a good buy for the price. I then read just about all 400 Amazon reviews and FINALLY made my purchase.
I ordered my Schwinn 430 from Amazon on 3/1/10 and it was delivered on 3/8/10. I was delighted that it was delivered so fast and also happy about the free shipping.
My machine was delivered by ABF Freight Co. I know that some reviewers have complained about the shipping company but I had no problems at all. The driver was wonderful. He took the box down a small hill to the back of my house, up two steps onto the deck and then into the house. He was great!!!!!
It took Tom about 1-1/2 to 2 hours to put the machine together. He had just recently put together his Sole and so the parts were recognizable to him although I nearly passed out when I saw the photo of all the parts in the manual. Tom said that the manual was straight forward although there was an addendum for a particular washer. We didn't see that until I said "hey, what's this piece of paper saying?" All the pieces were accounted for and all the holes lined up perfectly. He used some of his own tools but used the supplied allen wrench where indicated. We didn't lube the parts as recommended by some reviewers.
I've used it for 3 days now and there is not a squeak to be heard, except for the creaking of my knees. I'm 5'7" and about 150 lbs and the 18" stride is fine for me. I'm a former runner and in good shape (I thought). I have the elliptical on level 1 and after 20 minutes, I've worked up a good sweat.
I agree that a backlight for the computer would have been nice but it's not a deal breaker for me. The 6 programs are more than enough.
I think this machine is well made and feels very solid. There is no rocking or moving. I have it on a carpet and did not buy a mat. I love that it has a small footprint. The longer machines would not have fit into the space alloted for the elliptical. For the price, it can't be beat. I highly recommend it.
I'll post again in a month to let you know if there is any squeaking. It's been almost 3 months now and I still love the machine. No squeaking at all. Good workout and still happy with my purchase. It did develop a squish (not a squeak) but then worked itself out.
text_fidelity_b: Schwinn Fitness 430 Elliptical Trainer [Discontinued]

text_fidelity_a:
Freeze Dried Sliced Strawberries by Nutristore | Pack of 2 | Healthy Snack | Emergency Survival Bulk Food Storage | Amazing Taste & Quality | 25 Year Shelf Life These strawberries are beyond delicious! These big #10 (one gallon) cans of freeze dried fruit are IDEAL if you are new to using freeze dried fruits or if you want to put away a couple cans for your family in case of emergency but you don't want to spend $150 on a 6 can case plus shipping from somewhere else. (You simply cannot beat Amazon Prime!)

• • • #10 cans typically hold 12 cups of food and about 11 cups of freeze dried fruits and veggies • • •

It is hard to find information about how much food is actually in a #10 can and have it be accurate enough that you can plan your meals. When filled to the brim with something like rice, the #10 cans hold 12 cups. But freeze dried food is light and not compacted, with air space between the dry pieces so you get about 11 cups (bananas) to 11.25 cups (strawberries and raspberries) in a big can like this. The cans are "full", the difference is simply air space between the fruit pieces. (To be safe, always assume there are 11 cups per #10 can of freeze dried fruits and veggies. I have found this to be accurate and a great way to calculate how much you have stored.)

Now let's talk about how yummy the food is! As I took pictures I could hardly stop my 9 year old son from grabbing handfuls of strawberries behind my back as I tried to snap a quick photo. (The bowl of strawberries was dumped straight into his mouth mere seconds after I got that picture!) The fruit is positively DELICIOUS for snacking straight from the can!

We live in Houston and personally lived through Hurricane Ike in 2008. At the time my son was 18 months old and I would have given anything - ANYTHING - to have these freeze dried strawberries to have offered him. Grocery stores were picked clean the day before the storm. Some of the grocery stores flooded and most of them had damage to roofs, glass doors and building structures from being hit by flung tree branches, fence pieces and debris. We went 12 days without electricity in our home. Grocery stores were without power for the first 5 or 6 days and stayed closed for about a week in our area as they had to be cleaned up before reopening. It was almost 3 weeks after the storm before stores were restocked with fresh produce beyond a few local items like tomatoes and jalapeños. Please, take the advice from someone who has lived through a natural disaster and invest in freeze dried fruits and veggies for your family. Everything in our refrigerators and freezers were ruined by day 2 without power and we still had 10 days to go. The only thing you have to rely on is what you have on your pantry shelves. That is it. These cans will keep for 25 years unopened and truly are a wise investment.

So, since I have been through a natural disaster, I have learned how to bake with freeze dried food since I still live in Houston and may have to deal with another storm in the future. These strawberries did GREAT and I'm going to include the recipe I used so you can have success with them, too. It is wise to open and try the food you are storing but since this company gave several reviewers like myself a discount to test their products, this work has been done for you. You can simply store the cans of food knowing it is superior quality. (I have purchased and used Thrive brand fruits and these taste identical to theirs! In my opinion these strawberries were even better quality.)

• Strawberry Chocolate Chip Muffins •
--> This recipe also works with freeze dried blueberries or other freeze dried fruits
1/4 cup butter, softened
1/3 cup sugar
1 egg, beaten
1/2 cup milk (a small can of evaporated milk is fine to use)
1 cup flour (up to 1.5 cups depending on humidity; batter should be a thick muffin batter)
1 and 1/2 tsp baking powder
1/2 cup freeze dried strawberries (or raspberries or other fruit) rehydrated in 1/2 cup water with the excess liquid drained off
1/2 cup milk chocolate chips

Preheat oven to 400°. Cream butter and sugar. Add the egg and mix well. Add flour alternately with splashes of milk and combine until a thick batter has formed and all ingredients are incorporated. Gently fold in rehydrated fruit. Spoon into 12 paper lined baking cups, filling halfway to 3/4ths full. Bake for 20 minutes or until tops begin to turn golden.

• Tip •
The leftover powder at the bottom of each can is AWESOME for making strawberry butter or adding to oatmeal to make your own fruit and cream flavor. If nothing else, dump the powder in your pancake batter. Don't let the powder go to waste, it is delicious!

Also, if you want to know about the countries of origin on the fruits, this was posted on the seller's FAQ page: "We source our Nutristore foods from some of the following countries: USA, Canada, Ecuador, Greece, Costa Rica, Uruguay, Argentina, Serbia, New Zealand, India, Poland, Mexico & Chile. [We] no longer source foods from China."

I was very fortunate to be able to purchase this pack of freeze dried strawberries at a discount so I could try it, eat it and bake with it before writing a review. I hope that by sharing my photos and experience that you are able to make the best buying decision for your own family! Hugs from Houston!
